messages:
Alex: Heads-up — marketplace asked for a chain-of-custody record for SOC reports + pen artifacts before the listing goes live. We need a minimal provenance CSV and a single owner for each artifact.
Sam: I can take ownership of pen-test provenance. Do we have a template for fields we need? :thinking_face:
Maria: Not yet. Suggest columns: artifact_id, type (SOC/pen/qa), origin (vendor/team), upload_time_utc, uploader, checksum_sha256, storage_uri, access_policy, retention_days, approval_signature, note.
Jordan: That looks good. Add `related_ticket` and `confidence_level` (low/med/high) so marketplace reviewers can triage.
Alex: Good call. Let's keep it compact. We need two flows: 1) SI/partner-provided artifacts (they upload to our secure bucket) 2) Redwood-generated artifacts (we attach provenance automatically).
Sam: For partner uploads I propose we issue expiring upload tokens scoped to a partner folder and require checksum + manifest.csv. Example token ttl: 12h.
Maria: Agree. Also require a short attestation text from the partner for each artifact (who collected it and when). We'll capture that in `note` + `approval_signature` (signed email or SAML assertion).
Alex: Who can own the partner onboarding checklist and confirm partners can produce the attestation? 
Maria: I'll handle partner onboarding checklist and coordinate with SI leads. I'll create a quick sheet.
Sam: I'll implement the artifact manifest validation (checksum + schema) and make a small lambda to verify and move to long-term storage with a generated provenance record.
Jordan: Compliance: I will review retention_days and approval_signature requirements. Also set minimum retention to 2 years for SOC reports, 1 year for pen artifacts, unless legal says otherwise.
Alex: Timeline: we need this wired for the listing review in 7 business days. Actions: Maria — partner checklist + sample attestation (due EOD +3); Sam — validation lambda + manifest schema (EOD +4); Jordan — retention policy + sign-off (EOD +5). I'll draft a short message for marketplace reviewers explaining our provenance process.
Maria: Quick Q — for `storage_uri` format, do we prefer s3://redwood-marketplace/<partner>/<artifact> or signed https? I'd lean s3 path + a short-lived public artifact link we can hand to reviewers.
Sam: Store canonical copy at s3 path. We can generate reviewer links that expire and log access. That way `storage_uri` is stable and reviewer link is ephemeral.
Jordan: Also log chain of access in CloudTrail and include an access_log pointer in the manifest if possible. Reviewers sometimes ask who accessed the file.
Alex: Perfect. One more: marketplace asked for provenance notarization for SOC PDFs (hash + timestamp). Sam — can your lambda also emit a notarization tuple {hash, utc_timestamp, issuer: "redwood-infra"}?
Sam: Yes. The lambda will compute sha256, store it in the manifest, and write a notarization entry to our audit table.
Maria: I'll add a column `notarization_id` to the manifest so we can reconcile.
Jordan: Heads-up on legal: if any partner artifacts contain sensitive PII we need to redact before handoff. Maria, please flag partners who might send raw logs.
Maria: Will do. I'll add a partner-level flag `may_contain_pii` in the onboarding checklist and require redaction or a redaction attestation.
Alex: Cool. Quick sample manifest header for validators to use (csv):
```
artifact_id,type,origin,upload_time_utc,uploader,checksum_sha256,storage_uri,access_policy,retention_days,approval_signature,related_ticket,confidence_level,notarization_id,note
```
Alex: Final ask — please drop status updates here as you complete items. If anyone hits blockers ping me + @jordan. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Automated scan reminder — please run `security/validate-manifest` after uploading artifacts (manual trigger available).
Sam: Noted. I'll post the manifest schema PR when ready.
Maria: Checklist draft in PR: partners/onboarding/marketplace-provenance.md — will ping when ready.
Jordan: I'll block time tomorrow to review the retention + legal bits.
Alex: Thanks team. This should cover the reviewers' ask and keep the listing on schedule.
